newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Two more die in accidents in Swiss Alps.
newsitem.headline: Two more die in accidents in Swiss Alps.

text.p: Two more persons have died in separate accidents in the Alps on Wednesday, Swiss police in Zermatt and the Engelberg regions said on Thursday.
Police in the canton of Wallis reported that an unidentified climber, believed to be Czech, plunged roughly 500 metres in an area of the Matterhorn's east wall. The body was recovered by helicopter.
Police in the canton of Obwalden said a mountain biker, thought to be a German, fell on a cliff face in the Engelberg area, possibly after losing his way in fog, and also died.
Swiss press reports at least 25 people had died in accidents in the Swiss Alps since mid-July. The latest deaths brought the death toll so far in the European Alps to nearly 50 in the past few weeks.
The sudden rise in the death toll was blamed in part on a break in the weather which was said to have led many climbers into the peaks.
New snow at higher altitudes has also created dangerous conditions.
